verdict.rationale: Sentry's Issues page and Trace Explorer support filtering/aggregating on arbitrary fields (e.g., impacted users, span attributes) via flexible ad-hoc queries, which aligns with grouping/filtering on high-cardinality fields without pre-defined schemas. However, the evidence never explicitly discusses cardinality limits, indexing requirements, or user id/request id specifically as a differentiator. missing for 10: explicit documentation on high-cardinality field handling (e.g., user id, request id) without pre-aggregation, performance/indexing guarantees, and independent hands-on confirmation of this specific capability.
